summary: This paper presents material assay results and radiation transport simulations for the QUTEbits collaboration's first deployment of superconducting qubits at SNOLAB, a deep underground facility providing $2$ km of rock shielding. Geant4 and G4CMP simulations predict a total background rate of $0.70$ mHz per Si chip in the shielded CUTE facility, dominated by bulk $^{238}$U and $^{232}$Th contamination, with calibration sources ($^{133}$Ba, $^{252}$Cf) allowing controlled radiation exposure studies.
motivation: Cosmic rays and environmental ionizing radiation cause decoherence and correlated errors in superconducting qubits, violating assumptions of quantum error correction schemes. Characterizing radiation effects in a controlled underground environment is essential to understand and mitigate radiation-induced qubit errors.
method: High-purity germanium spectroscopy assayed components to $\mathcal{O}(10\text{–}100)$ μBq/kg sensitivity. Measured radioactivities were propagated through Geant4 simulations of the CUTE geometry and shielding ($11$ cm lead, mu-metal, copper enclosures). G4CMP simulations of phonon and charge carrier dynamics in Si/Al devices determined phonon collection times ($\tau_{\mathrm{max}} \approx 14.7$ μs) and qubit hit multiplicities.
result: Bulk contamination yields $5.51 \times 10^{-1}$ mHz in Si chips and $7.78 \times 10^{1}$ mHz in Al cavities; $^{210}$Pb surface contamination from radon adds $\approx 0.14$ mHz to Si. External cavern radiation contributes $<8 \times 10^{-3}$ mHz. Calibration source rates reach $38.8 ± 5.8$ mHz ($^{133}$Ba, optimal angle) and $0.9 ± 0.3$ mHz ($^{252}$Cf), providing 7–50× excess over background. G4CMP shows energy deposits $\gtrsim 100$ eV cause correlated errors across all four transmon qubits on the $7 \times 7$ mm$^2$ chip.
